scalesUsed.notes: A - C - D - E - G - A
scalesUsed.application: Forms the entire harmonic and melodic vocabulary of the song (Am7 - Em7 - G - Am7 and the Dm7 turnaround)

scalesUsed.notes: A - B - C - D - E - F - G - A
scalesUsed.application: Provides smooth voice leading and soulful minor fills over the 12-bar-derived minor blues structure

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Intimate, stripped-back A minor soul-blues built on warm minor seventh voicings and deep rhythmic pocket
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: A minor is the relative minor of C major

mainProgression.progression: i7 - v7 - ♭VII - i7 | iv7 - v7 - i7
mainProgression.description: A compact variation on the 12-bar minor blues: the main vamp rocks between Am7, Em7, and G before stepping up to Em7 (v7) and Dm7 (iv7) for the turnaround.

sectionProgressions.section: Main Verse Vamp ('Ain't no sunshine when she's gone')
sectionProgressions.description: Fingerpicked acoustic bass-and-chord pulse that walks diatonically from A down to E and G
Classic minor-blues turnaround stepping from 7th-fret Em7 down to 5th-fret Dm7 and resolving back to Am7

sectionProgressions.section: Bridge ('I know, I know, I know...')
sectionProgressions.description: Iconic 26-count spoken/sung 'I know' breakdown where the guitar drops out completely before re-entering on the Dm7/Em7 cadence
Hypnotic repetition of the primary minor seventh groove fading into silence

harmonicFunction: Am7 (i7) - Warm, mellow minor seventh tonic voiced at the 5th fret or in open position
Em7 (v7) - Passing minor fifth chord that softens the traditional dominant pull
G (♭VII) - Subtonic chord walking the bass back up a whole step into the A minor root
Dm7 (iv7) - Subdominant minor seventh chord providing the emotional peak before resolving home

techniques.name: Fingerstyle Bass-Chord Plucking & Minor 7th Voicings
techniques.description: Using the thumb (p) to pluck root bass notes on the 6th and 5th strings while the index, middle, and ring fingers (i-m-a) pluck compact minor 7th triads on the D, G, and B strings

notes: Am7 (5th fret): 5-X-5-5-5-X
sequence: Pluck the 5th-fret Am7 chord on beats 1 and 2, then step down to Em7 on beat 3 and G on beat 4
Return to Am7 for a full bar, adding a gentle percussive thumb slap on beats 2 and 4
For the turnaround, slide up to Em7 (7th fret A string) for one bar, then Dm7 (5th fret A string) for one bar
Resolve back to the main Am7 - Em7 - G - Am7 vamp
tips: Keep the voicings warm and mellow by plucking with your fingertips rather than a sharp pick
Let the bass note land slightly ahead of or together with the three upper strings, followed by a deadened thumb tap on the low E string
Leave plenty of empty space—the silence between chords is what gives the song its haunting soul groove
details.progression: Am7 - Em7 - G - Am7 | Em7 - Dm7 - Am7

techniques.name: Percussive Thumb Slap & 5th-Position Blues Embellishments
techniques.description: Incorporating light rhythmic thumb taps against the lower strings on beats 2 and 4 to establish a steady soul pocket, while adding tasteful 5th-position A minor pentatonic hammer-ons

notes: Slap technique: The side of the picking thumb taps the 5th and 6th strings over the soundhole
Double-stop fill: Barring frets 5 on strings 3 and 4, hammering to fret 7 on string 4
Pocket timing: Keep the tempo laid-back at 78 BPM without dragging
sequence: Establish the rhythmic slap on beats 2 and 4 over a stationary Am7 chord
Insert short blues fills during the resting Am7 measure of each two-bar cycle
Maintain steady internal pulse during the 26-count tacet breakdown
Drop smoothly back into the groove right on beat 1 as Bill sings 'Anytime she goes away'
tips: Keep thumb slaps gentle; do not strike hard enough to make the acoustic top rattle
Use the flesh of the index finger to mute the high E string during double stops
Listen to Stephen Stills' subtle acoustic guitar nuances on the original recording

sections.name: Intro & Main Verse Vamp ('Ain't no sunshine when she's gone')
sections.description: Bill Withers and Stephen Stills' hypnotic Am7 - Em7 - G - Am7 acoustic soul-blues groove.
notes: Pluck the bass note with your thumb and the D, G, and B strings with your fingers
Make the Em7 to G transition on beats 3 and 4 smooth and unhurried
Rest on Am7 in the second measure of each two-bar phrase

sections.name: Minor Blues Turnaround ('Anytime she goes away')
sections.description: The soulful v7 to iv7 turnaround (Em7 - Dm7 - Am7) on 'Anytime she goes away'.
notes: Hold the A-string root Em7 shape at the 7th fret for four beats
Slide the exact same shape down two frets to Dm7 at the 5th fret
Return to the 5th-fret E-string Am7 vamp

sections.name: Verse 2 Subtle Dynamics & Walking Bass
sections.description: Second verse expanding the intimacy with light bass movement connecting the chords under Bill's narrative vocal.
notes: Subtle bass passing note on the low E string
Light thumb accents on downbeats
Keep vocal space wide open

sections.name: Bridge Breakdown ('I know, I know' 26-repetition pocket)
sections.description: The immortal 26-repetition vocal vamp where the guitar drops out completely while the strings and drums maintain the hypnotic pocket.
notes: Complete tacet on guitar
Maintain internal subdivision at 78 BPM
Prepare left hand for re-entry on Em7 turnaround

sections.name: Post-Breakdown Re-entry & Emotional Climax
sections.description: Explosive emotional release as Withers finishes his vocal flurry and the guitar crashes back in on the Em7 and Dm7 chords.
notes: Strong thumb attack on the 7th-fret Em7 downbeat
Full emotional commitment to the descending Dm7
Resonant resolution back to Am7

sections.name: Outro Vamp & Fade ('Anytime she goes away')
sections.description: Soulful outro vamp combining the two-bar chord cycle with delicate 5th-position double-stop embellishments as the song gently fades.
notes: Hammer-on from 5th to 7th fret on D string while barring G string
Gradual decrescendo as the track fades
Keep the volume soft and conversational

guitar.recommended: Martin D-28 or Gibson J-45 Acoustic Guitar (or Fender Stratocaster for electric soul versions)
guitar.pickup: Warm acoustic soundhole/condenser mic or Stratocaster neck single-coil pickup

amp.recommended: Acoustic DI / Fender Princeton Reverb (for electric/semi-hollow versions)

effects.other: Fingers (flesh of thumb and fingertips) for authentic soul warmth

beginner.title: Open Chords & Basic Vamp
steps: Practice the two-bar vamp: Am7 (beats 1-2), Em7 (beat 3), G (beat 4), Am7 (full bar)
Play through the verse and Em7 → Dm7 turnaround at 78 BPM

intermediate.title: 5th-Position Barre Voicings & Fingerstyle Slap
steps: Switch to the compact 4-string voicings at the 5th and 7th frets (Am7, Em7, Dm7)
Pluck the bass note with your thumb and upper strings with fingers i-m-a
Add a subtle percussive thumb slap on beats 2 and 4 during the resting Am7 bar

advanced.title: Chord-Melody & Pentatonic Pocket Fills
steps: Weave 5th-position A minor pentatonic double-stop fills into the second bar of Am7 without losing the groove
Hold the silent pocket during the 26-count 'I know' breakdown and re-enter on the exact beat
Perform as a solo vocal-and-guitar arrangement

commonMistakes: Strumming all six strings aggressively with a pick, which ruins the intimate soul vibe
Rushing the Em7 → G walk on beats 3 and 4
Overplaying during the resting Am7 bar instead of letting the groove breathe
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: Fingerstyle Am7 → Em7 → G → Am7 vamp at 70 BPM → 78 BPM
5 minutes: 7th-fret Em7 to 5th-fret Dm7 turnaround shifts
5 minutes: Adding one tasteful A minor pentatonic fill at the end of every second Am7 bar
5 minutes: Full song playthrough with vocal phrasing
focusAreas: Warm fingerstyle tone balance between thumb and fingers
Seamless transition from chord plucking to pentatonic fills
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 78 BPM and feel the click as beats 2 and 4 (like a soul snare backbeat)
Practice the Em7 (beat 3) to G (beat 4) movement so it sits slightly behind the beat
Count through the 'I know' breakdown with the metronome clicking
